author: Mark Atwood
text:
Workspace-architectural decision needed. Two options presented without recommendation in bead body = direct human-needed per workspace AGENTS.md "When NOT to file human" rule 3 qualifier ("two equally-plausible options presented without a recommendation").

**Verification (2026-05-18):**
- tasks-server/src/backend.rs:209 — `fn is_per_user_property(prop: &str) -> bool { ... }` IS a trait associated function (no &self). Backends override per-impl at compile time. Has spec-anchored default body.
- calendars-server/src/backend.rs:295 rustdoc references `jmap_calendars_types::is_per_user_calendar_event_property` — free function in types crate. NO backend override seam.

Bead premise verified accurate.

**Workspace-policy signals (neither decisive):**

Argument for option (a) — predicate-on-backend-trait (tasks shape):
- Workspace AGENTS.md "Caller identity (foundation seam)": "backends are canonical for permission enforcement". Per-user-property routing is adjacent to permission-enforcement and benefits from the same canonical placement.
- Workspace AGENTS.md extras-preservation policy: every wire struct ships `extra: serde_json::Map<...>`. A vendor that adds `acmeCorpUserState` as a per-user vendor field MUST be able to declare it per-user-scoped, or the workspace extras-preservation policy is undermined for this routing decision specifically. Option (b) (predicate in types crate) gives vendors no extensibility hook here.
- The Filter-algebra exclusion section says "silent-drop is a server-side query-correctness bug". A vendor field that gets misrouted (treated as shared state when intended as per-user) is the same shape of correctness bug. Option (a) lets vendors prevent this; option (b) does not.

Argument for option (b) — predicate-in-types-crate (calendars shape):
- "Is property X per-user?" is a spec-defined static classification, not a backend behavior. The spec authoritatively lists which properties are per-user (draft-tasks-06 §4.5.1, draft-ietf-jmap-calendars-26 §5.10.2 or whichever).
- Putting it in the types crate gives kit-author canonical control over spec evolution: when the spec adds a new per-user property in a future draft revision, ONE update to the types crate reaches every backend.
- Backends overriding the predicate to disagree with the spec is itself a spec-violating bug; the override seam tempts backends into that bug.

**Slight tilt toward option (a)** because the extras-preservation policy specifically requires vendor extensibility on related routing decisions, and the workspace already names "backends are canonical" for adjacent concerns. But this is a real workspace decision and the kit-author has standing reasons to prefer (b) (spec-evolution control). Filing human for the explicit call.

**Cross-coupling notes:**
- This decision blocks adding per-user-property semantics to contacts-server, filenode-server, and any future extension-server siblings. They should adopt whichever shape this bead resolves to from day one.
- The new "spec-mandated-method default impl" workspace question being decided under JMAP-ic0j.26 / JMAP-ops7.23 / JMAP-ops7.24 is related: both touch the question of "what goes on the backend trait vs elsewhere". The two questions could plausibly resolve together as a single workspace-traits-shape epic.
